exactness_argument.indexbuild: The derived producer differs from the row's in three computations, none of which changes a value. (1) State loop: S3Solver128::roots computes prepare, one inversion of the denominator a*ps (zero takes the scalar fallback) and finish. RootBatch128::solve computes the same prepare, inverts the product of the row's non-zero denominators once and recovers each inverse as (prefix product) x (inverse of the running product), which is that denominator's field inverse because inverses in GF(2^83) are unique; finish then returns the same two roots in the same order. States are pushed in the parent's (left, right, relative) order, so stored_states_blake3 is the parent's. (2) Insert loop: index_canonical128 is a pure function of the root (plus the planted counter, called once per root in the same order), so computing it 32 roots early changes no key or shift; the prefetch is a hint without architectural effect; insert_if_absent is called with the same (key, value) sequence into the same table, so every slot word, and table_slots_blake3, is the parent's. (3) Self-test: the parent returns false iff some image of [0, domain) is >= domain or an in-range image repeats, else visited == len; the lanes loop evaluates the same apply on the same indices and the same checks on the images in index order, eight applies ahead of their checks, so it returns the same boolean. Relations, probes, the rank stage and the online scan read only the index and the self-test verdict, so they are the parent's. Gated per process and per base on K600, M38 and M10.
exactness_argument.parent: Frobenius phi acts on the prime-order subgroup as multiplication by lambda (lambda^2 - lambda + 2 = 0 mod r), so for alpha = a + b tau, alpha(R) = [a]R + [b]phi(R) = [(a + b lambda) mod r]R, and every member +-phi^k(alpha(R_c)) of orbit (c, alpha) has discrete log +-(a + b lambda) lambda^k log R_c. The header carries exactly these labels; verify_closure.py re-derives every member and label from the orbit representative and checks each representative against [w]R_c and, with the table, against [w L_c]G, in the pinned oracle. A relation found by the unchanged S3 search is checked in the group by the unchanged lift (four base points summing to the attempt's point), so its row sum_i coeff_i L_{c_i} = a (+ L_c for the guided column) holds exactly; full rank gives the unique logs, checked [L_c]G = R_c in process and equal to B's archived logs of the same R_c. A target's scalar is checked [d]G = Q in process and replayed in the oracle, and must equal the baseline's and the tuned rho's. The root index, probe loop and scan are the rank-probe producer's code, built from the closure's orbit representatives. With KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift the index build keys every stored state's two normal-basis roots with lift_scan instead of the selected canonicalizer; both return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift reaching it, the stored states are computed before and independently of that call, so the table receives the same inserts in the same order and its slot array is the same word for word (index-lift's argument). The layout digests gate this per process on every base, so every relation, probe count, rank table and scalar of a lift-built index is the selected-built index's.

question: Is the derived index-build producer's END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) on the M38 closure base lower than the current n=83 a=1 row's (the closure + index-lift M38I producer), on new held-out points and new rank seeds? The derived producer builds the same root index (the same stored states, slot words, relations and probes) with one field inversion per state row and a prefetched look-ahead insert loop, and computes the same exhaustive scan self-test eight images at a time. The test uses repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound must exceed 1 (AGENTS.md, 'CPU performance isolation gate', Tier 1).

why_this_run: On the Tier 1 template run 39359922687 (PR #1002) side B (this experiment's side A) spent about 15.6 of its 21.7 s end to end in the index build and 1.7 s in the scan self-test; the rank stage is 3.7 s. A local profile (inputs/local_profile.json, diagnostic) puts about 6.5 s of a 16.9 s build in one field inversion per stored state and about 5.3 s in the table insert's cache, TLB and first-touch misses.
